summary: deposit-limit-fe postinstall exfiltrates installer identity via DNS beacon and native addon POST to bare IP
details: On npm install, postinstall.js issues a DNS lookup for a subdomain of the form `<hostname>.<package>.db4jlbku53082dmp0d7g3mffj7s7aordk.oast.me`, leaking the installer's hostname and the npm package name to an out-of-band collaborator domain. It then require()'s a precompiled Linux x64 native addon at `prebuilds/linux-x64/addon.node`, which contains hardcoded destination `64.181.165.115`, a `POST /dc HTTP/1.0` request, and the format string `h=%.60s&u=%.30s&p=%.50s&r=%.100s`; the binary reads `gethostname`, `getpwuid`/`getuid`, `npm_package_name`, and `npm_config_registry` and transmits them to that IP. The package ships only an index.js stub, the postinstall script, and the opaque ELF addon — no source, no binding.gyp, and no native-build tooling — so the binary's sole observed role at install time is identity exfiltration to a bare-IP endpoint over cleartext HTTP.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
